items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: I wasn’t here but this is what I was told. Lucky Roberts played and jammed all night

ctx.x: Yeah. Art Tatum I think worked at the library. He would play his gig. The gig was just a means to the end but the real music would come to the after night sessions. He would go for the sessions. I wasn’t here but this is what I was told. Lucky Roberts played and jammed all night where they would cut heads and that naturally the baddest cat played last and then he would leave and go take a shower or whatever and go and do his regular job during the day at the library or something. So a whole lot of people had day…
What was the impact of the civil rights movement and then the civil rights bill in ’64 or whatever. Did it make any difference in your life?
